children: Westpac's bear at Morgan Stanley sees downside risk to both earnings and trading multiples despite strong growth in business lending, good cost control and sound credit quality. Analyst Richard E. Wiles sees several positives at the Australian bank, but warns that its most recent fiscal half showed weakness in mortgages and soft margins. He tells clients in a note that he is more confident in Westpac's ability to control costs, but margin pressure will mean FY 2027 revenue growth significantly lags volume growth. MS keeps an underweight rating on the stock and raises its target price 3.3% to 31.00 Australian dollars. Shares are down 0.2% at A$37.105. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
